List helpers

Source: R/camera.R, R/point_cloud.R, R/utils_misc.R
list_helpers.Rd

Ports of manim.utils.iterables, working on R vectors and lists (atomic input gives atomic output). Elements compare as in Python: mobjects and other environments by identity, everything else by value.

Usage

extract_mobject_family_members(
  mobjects = mobject_list,
  use_z_index = FALSE,
  only_those_with_points = FALSE,
  mobject_list = NULL
)

stretch_array_to_length(nparray, length)

adjacent_n_tuples(objects, n)

adjacent_pairs(objects)

all_elements_are_instances(iterable, Class)

concatenate_lists(...)

list_difference_update(l1, l2, key = NULL)

list_update(l1, l2, key = NULL)

listify(obj)

tuplify(obj)

make_even(iterable_1, iterable_2)

make_even_by_cycling(iterable_1, iterable_2)

remove_list_redundancies(lst)

remove_nones(sequence)

resize_array(nparray, length)

resize_preserving_order(nparray, length)

resize_with_interpolation(nparray, length)

batch_by_property(items, property_func)

uniq_chain(...)

flatten_iterable_parameters(args)

restructure_list_to_exclude_certain_family_members(mobject_list, to_remove)

hash_obj(obj)

Arguments

mobjects, mobject_list, to_remove

Lists of mobjects.

use_z_index

Sort the result by z_index.

only_those_with_points

Keep only mobjects that have points.

nparray

A vector or matrix.

length

Length of the result.

objects, iterable, iterable_1, iterable_2, lst, sequence, l1, l2, obj, items

A vector or list.

n

Window size.

Class

A class name or R6 class generator.

...

Vectors or lists.

key

NULL, or a function giving the value elements compare by.

property_func

Function giving the property of an item.

args

A list.

Value

A list or a vector, as described above for each function. all_elements_are_instances() returns TRUE or FALSE, and hash_obj() returns a hash string.

Details

  • adjacent_n_tuples(objects, n): the length(objects) windows of n cyclically consecutive elements; adjacent_pairs() uses n = 2.

  • all_elements_are_instances(iterable, Class): whether every element inherits from Class (a class name or an R6 class generator).

  • concatenate_lists(...): all elements of the arguments, in order.

  • list_difference_update(l1, l2, key): the elements of l1 that are not in l2; list_update(l1, l2, key) appends l2 to that, so elements of l2 move to the end. With key, elements compare by key(element).

  • listify(obj) and tuplify(obj): obj as a list; a single string is one element, a mobject gives its submobjects (R has no tuples, so both return a list).

  • make_even(iterable_1, iterable_2): both stretched to the longer length by repeating elements in place; make_even_by_cycling() repeats them cyclically. Each returns a list of the two results.

  • remove_list_redundancies(lst): drops repeated elements, keeping the last occurrence of each.

  • remove_nones(sequence): drops elements that are false in Python's sense (NULL, FALSE, 0, "", empty vectors, and mobjects without submobjects), as upstream's if x filter does.

  • stretch_array_to_length(nparray, length): a vector, or a matrix by rows, stretched to length entries by repeating them in place; it is an error to shrink.

  • resize_array(nparray, length): a vector, or a matrix by rows, cut or cyclically repeated to length entries (as numpy.resize). resize_preserving_order() repeats or drops entries in place instead, and resize_with_interpolation() interpolates linearly between neighboring entries.

  • batch_by_property(items, property_func): consecutive items with the same property_func(item) grouped; a list of list(batch, property) pairs.

  • uniq_chain(...): the elements of all arguments in order, without repeats.

  • hash_obj(obj): a hash (a string) of a nested list that does not depend on the order of the entries of named lists.

  • flatten_iterable_parameters(args): the elements of args, with those that are themselves lists or vectors of several elements spliced in (one level).

  • extract_mobject_family_members(mobjects, use_z_index, only_those_with_points): every member of the families of the mobjects, once each, optionally sorted by z_index and without the members that have no points. mobject_list (the name in manim.utils.family_ops) is accepted for mobjects. restructure_list_to_exclude_certain_family_members(mobject_list, to_remove) drops to_remove and their family from the list; a group that holds one of them is replaced by its remaining members.

Examples

adjacent_pairs(1:4)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 1 2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 2 3
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] 3 4
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> [1] 4 1
#> 
list_update(c(1, 2, 3, 4), c(2, 5))
#> [1] 1 3 4 2 5
make_even(1:3, 4:8)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 1 1 2 2 3
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 4 5 6 7 8
#> 
remove_list_redundancies(c(1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 4))
#> [1] 1 3 2 4
